policy_title: Support First-Time Buyers and Improve Building Standards
stated: Labour will work with local authorities to give first-time buyers the initial opportunity to purchase homes in new developments, preventing sales to international investors before construction is complete. A permanent, comprehensive mortgage guarantee scheme will be introduced to support first-time buyers with lower mortgage costs due to smaller deposits. The party will also ensure more high-quality, well-designed, and sustainable homes are built, implement solutions to unlock building affected by nutrient neutrality, and improve building safety, protecting leaseholders from costs and accelerating remediation.

source.quote: Labour will work with local authorities to give first-time buyers the first chance to buy homes and end the farce of entire developments being sold off to international investors before houses are even built. And we will introduce a permanent, comprehensive mortgage guarantee scheme, to support first-time buyers who struggle to save for a large deposit, with lower mortgage costs. Labour wants exemplary development to be the norm not the exception. We will take steps to ensure we are building more high-quality, well-designed, and sustainable homes and creating places that increase climate resilience and promote nature recovery. We will implement solutions to unlock the building of homes affected by nutrient neutrality without weakening environmental protections. Labour will also take decisive action to improve building safety, including through regulation, to ensure we never again see a repeat of the Grenfell fire. We will review how to better protect leaseholders from costs and take steps to accelerate the pace of remediation across the country. We will put a renewed focus on ensuring those responsible for the building safety crisis pay to put it right.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets housing affordability and supply via first-time buyer priority over investors, a permanent mortgage guarantee scheme to lower deposit barriers, and measures to unlock and increase the volume of new homes built.

Explicitly unlocking building blocked by nutrient neutrality rules has a real, non-negligible bearing on water quality — the environmental protection mechanism exists precisely to prevent excess nutrient runoff into waterways, so any solution (mitigation or relaxation) materially affects that indicator.

A 'permanent, comprehensive' mortgage guarantee creates an open-ended contingent government liability; in the event of a housing-market downturn and rising defaults, the exchequer must cover losses—a specific fiscal mechanism that the OBR and IFS treat as a non-negligible off-balance-sheet risk at scale.

membership_note: Three fundamentals bear real verdicts: O1 is the primary design target; O6 arises from the nutrient-neutrality unlock as a concrete environmental tradeoff; O12 arises from the permanent contingent fiscal liability of the guarantee scheme. Effects on O2, O14, and O13 are either subsumed in O1 or too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
